annotation.kind: source-faithful Banach-algebra formulation of both power-series bounds in Theorem 4.2

assumptions: The complex Banach algebra specializes to the paper's finite complex matrix algebra with a submultiplicative norm.
The coefficients below ell vanish, matching the tail power series h_ell.
The nonnegative scalar r bounds the indicated generator-power norms; choosing r as the paper's maximum of the corresponding power roots gives these hypotheses.
The absolute scalar majorant is summable, which is the formal convergence condition used in place of the paper's radius-of-convergence notation.
For part (b), coefficients of non-even powers vanish.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P25 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P25 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p25_t3_theorem4_2 (c : Nat -> Complex) (A : E) (p ell : Nat) (hp : 0 < p) (hcutoff : forall k < ell, c k = 0) : the ordinary p,p+1 bound and the even 2p,2p+2 bound both imply P25SeriesBound
formal_statement.plain_language: A matrix power series supported from degree ell is bounded by its absolute scalar series using only the pth and (p+1)st power norms once ell is at least p(p-1); if the series is even, the analogous bound uses the 2pth and (2p+2)nd power norms once ell is at least 2p(p-1).

informal_proof: Use quotient and remainder modulo p to express every k at least p(p-1) as (p+1)m1+pm2. Submultiplicativity transfers the two generator-power bounds to every supported power. For the even case apply the same argument to A squared. Bound each series term, obtain absolute summability, and pass the pointwise bound through the infinite sum.
informal_statement: Both parts of Theorem 4.2: the tail matrix power series admits the practical p,p+1 norm bound, and an even series admits the sharper 2p,2p+2 bound.

absence_search.result: The importable frozen NumStability set has no supported matrix-power-series norm theorem, no consecutive-generator exponent theorem, and no even-series analogue of Theorem 4.2. Generic matrix powers, submultiplicative infinity-norm bounds, and matrix-exponential trace interfaces do not prove this target.

tier_rationale: The proof must build a quotient-remainder numerical-semigroup representation, lift two generator bounds through noncommutative power and norm algebra, handle the even specialization through A squared, establish absolute summability, and control an infinite Banach-algebra series. This is substantial T2-or-harder work. NumStability has no corresponding result, so L receives no material advantage over N.
